nodes.summary: Let $F$ be the free group on $x, y$, viewed inside the free group on $x, y, t$. The base relators are the elements $[[a, b], [c, d]]$ and $[a, b]^2$ for all $a, b, c, d \in F$.
nodes.title: Base relators of the Kropholler group

nodes.summary: The Kropholler group $G$ is the group with generators $x, y, t$ whose relators are the base relators, namely $[[a, b], [c, d]]$ and $[a, b]^2$ for all $a, b, c, d$ in the free group $F$ on $x, y$, together with the twist relators $t x t^{-1} y^{-1}$ and $t y t^{-1} (x y)^{-1}$.
nodes.title: The Kropholler group

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be the Kropholler group. Then $H^4(G, M) \neq 0$ for some $\mathbb{Q}G$-module $M$, and $H^n(G, M) = 0$ for every $\mathbb{Q}G$-module $M$ and every integer $n > 4$. This resolves Kourovka Notebook Problem 12.41 by P. H. Kropholler, which asks whether this cohomological dimension is 3 or 4.
nodes.title: The Kropholler group has rational cohomological dimension 4

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be the Kropholler group. This is the proposition that $H^4(G, M) \neq 0$ for some $\mathbb{Q}G$-module $M$, and $H^n(G, M) = 0$ for every $\mathbb{Q}G$-module $M$ and every integer $n > 4$; that is, the cohomological dimension of $G$ over $\mathbb{Q}$ is $4$.
nodes.title: Rational cohomological dimension 4 of the Kropholler group (Kourovka 12.41)

nodes.summary: In the free group on $x, y, t$, the twist relators are the two elements $t x t^{-1} y^{-1}$ and $t y t^{-1} (x y)^{-1}$; they encode the relations $t x t^{-1} = y$ and $t y t^{-1} = x y$, so conjugation by $t$ acts as the automorphism $\varphi \colon x \mapsto y,\ y \mapsto x y$.
nodes.title: Twist relators of the Kropholler group
